The NiCrAlY bond coating was 0.003 to 0.008 cm thick, and the stabilized zirconia thermal barrier coatings were 0.025 to 0.064 cm thick.
The ZrO2-12Y2O3 coating was primarily cubic in structure, while the ZrO2-3.4MgO was also primarily cubic and the ZrO2-5.4CaO had a mix of cubic and monoclinic phases.
Failures of the ZrO2-MgO and ZrO2-CaO coatings occurred within the oxide layer near the bond coating interface.
The ZrO2-12Y2O3 coating showed the best adherence, thermal shock resistance, and resistance to cracking compared to the other coatings tested.
The Mach 0.3 burner rig tests produced very high thermal gradients up to 500°C/cm on the surface and 645°C through the 0.064 cm thick ZrO2-12Y2O3 coating.
The ZrO2-12Y2O3 coating withstood 3200 cycles (80 sec at 1280°C) and 275 cycles (1 hr at 1490°C) without cracking or spalling.
Increasing the ZrO2-12Y2O3 coating thickness from 0.051 to 0.064 cm improved the crack resistance and adherence without adversely affecting performance.
The ZrO2-12Y2O3 coating lost about 50% of its thickness after 246 cycles (1 hr at 1410°C), 182 cycles (1 hr at 1440°C), and 158 cycles (1 hr at 1480°C).
